system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:51:18 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 sent 51,000,468 bytes to the explicit proxy at 10.30.20.30:8080 over a 15-second connection. This establishes a large client-to-proxy transfer, but the record does not identify its external destination or contents.

At 14:17 UTC, the proxy recorded maria.lopez connecting to drive.google.com. Google Drive is not among the organization's approved file-sharing services, but this later, short tunnel does not establish that it was related to the 13:51 transfer.

An Explorer UserAssist registry entry contains a ROT13-encoded path that decodes to powershell.exe. This is consistent with PowerShell having been recorded in UserAssist, but does not provide a command line or link PowerShell to the large transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor coverage information reports that WS-MLOPEZ-01 winsec and Sysmon logs, and proxy logs, were not collected from 13:30 through 14:10 UTC because of a collection outage.
The large-transfer record identifies the workstation-to-proxy connection and byte counts, but does not show the proxied destination, request details, or transferred content.
The later Google Drive proxy event occurs after the stated outage window; it does not resolve what destination or activity accounted for the transfer at 13:51.
claims_not_established: The external destination, URL, or service associated with the 13:51 transfer.
Whether the transferred bytes were an upload of files or other data, and what their contents were.
Which process or user action generated the 13:51 transfer.
Whether the 14:17 Google Drive access involved an upload or was related to the earlier large transfer.
Whether the transfer was authorized business activity or malicious exfiltration.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain proxy logs for 13:30–14:10 UTC, including CONNECT and request details, user attribution, upstream destination, and byte counts for the 13:51 connection.
Obtain endpoint EDR or recovered Sysmon and winsec telemetry for WS-MLOPEZ-01 during the outage, especially process creation, command lines, file access, and network attribution around 13:51.
Review firewall, proxy-upstream, DNS, and TLS metadata that could identify the destination and nature of the transfer.

Check Google Drive or other relevant cloud-service audit records for uploads associated with maria.lopez or WS-MLOPEZ-01 around the alert window, and confirm with the user whether the activity was expected.
